classification.difficultyReason: Standardise one threshold, use the table and its complement, then express the result as a percentage.

content.prompt:
A study found mean cholesterol level 219 mg/mL with standard deviation 41 mg/mL for adult males without heart disease. Assume cholesterol levels in this population are normally distributed.

Doctors classify a reading above 240 mg/mL as high.

What percentage of this population has high cholesterol? Use the standard normal table and give your answer to the nearest whole percent.

answer.worked:
Let $X$ be the cholesterol level in mg/mL.

$$\begin{aligned}z&=\frac{240-219}{41}\\z&=\frac{21}{41}\\z&\approx0.51\end{aligned}$$

From the standard normal table, $P(Z\le0.51)=0.6950$.

$$\begin{aligned}P(X>240)&\approx P(Z>0.51)\\P(X>240)&\approx1-0.6950\\P(X>240)&\approx0.3050\end{aligned}$$

The percentage is approximately $0.3050\times100\%=30.50\%$, or $31\%$ to the nearest whole percent.
